transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-31
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Rodriguez (CTO - Galactic Insights), Marcus Yoon (SRE), Priya Shah (Head ML), Derek Lim (VP Eng)

Summary:
Galactic Insights is evaluating Redwood Dedicated reserved GPU pools to support a new real-time insights product. Primary constraints: finance/quarterly billing alignment, strict isolation for PII/financial datasets, burst up to 10x on product launch windows, and an SLO of p95 latency < 120ms for short text generation paths. They want pricing scenarios that align with their fiscal cycles and a bench plan to validate warm-pool prewarm vs on-demand fallback.

Topics covered:
- Reserved capacity pricing and quarter-aligned billing
- Tenant isolation and VPC/KMS requirements (PCI-like controls)
- Warm pool / prewarm strategy and eviction tolerance
- Fallback to hosted variants and automatic model downgraders
- Bench/POC plan and next technical deep dive

Action items (captured in metadata): Maya will send pricing; Omar will plan bench; Marcus to provide traffic profile.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, and with me is omar our se. nice to meet you all. quick intros?
[00:12] Lena: lena here, cto at galactic insights. we do fast-turn financial event summarization for traders, so low latency matters and also retention and auditability.
[00:22] Derek: derek, vp eng, i'm here for procurement/ops alignment, mainly the billing cadence question.
[00:28] Marcus: marcus, s r e. i'll own integration anomalies, prewarming, and failover.
[00:33] Priya: priya, head of ml, model infra and quality gates.
[00:39] Omar: great, thanks. quick agenda — qualify workloads, constraints, isolation, burst profiles, then pricing/next steps. sound good?
[00:47] Lena: yep.

[01:02] Maya: lena, can you describe the main workload? qps, typical sequence lengths, and peak windows?
[01:11] Lena: so two main paths — a short path for headline gen, typically 20-40 tokens, and a long path for full summarization ~300 tokens. baseline qps is about 40 rps, but during earnings windows we see spikes to roughly 400 rps sustained for 10-20 minutes and occasional microbursts up to 1k rps for ~60s.
[01:35] Omar: hmm okay that maps to a steady baseline with big spikes. what's your current evictions tolerance and availability needs?
[01:42] Marcus: we can't afford dropped requests during spikes, would rather have graceful degradation — e.g., auto-fallback to smaller model variant or hosted fallback — but we need audit logs and data never leave our VPC for the long-path summaries.
[01:57] Maya: good note on data residency. for Dedicated Private we support VPC and on-prem options; dedicated can be configured to keep long-path models in your private cluster while allowing short-path to use a cheaper hosted variant when needed.

[02:20] Priya: is that mean the KV cache can be private too? Session caching and prefix caching are important for latency.
[02:28] Omar: yes the KV cache is co-located in the dedicated runtime. we can pin the cache to reserved nodes and expose policies for sticky warm-pools. caveat: warm-pools incur cost while reserved.

[02:45] Derek: speaking of cost — our procurement needs quarterly billing alignment. we have budget room each quarter not a big annual commitment. can you do quarterly reserved commitments?
[02:56] Maya: yes we can do monthly or multi-month commits; quarterly invoicing is common for customers in finance. Will put together scenarios: monthly pay-as-you-go, 3-month reserve with discount, and 12-month reserve options.

[03:14] Lena: what's the uplift from baseline if we prewarm vs relying on on-demand burst?
[03:20] Omar: prewarm reduces cold-start token latency significantly; in our internal tests prewarm eliminated a 200–400ms cold-start for the larger models, which matters for p95. But it's cost tradeoff — warm-pool capacity is charged even if idle. we can model probabilistic burst windows to size warm-pools efficiently. i can show a modeling sheet.
[03:42] Maya: (referring) shared doc: https://redwood.example.com/docs/galactic-burst-modeling — will include in follow-up.

[04:00] Marcus: for compliance, we need KMS/HSM integration and audit trails for tokens and model versions. also SOC2 plus quarterly vulnerability scans. do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:11] Omar: yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). audit logs are available in the console with retention options; for Private we can integrate with your on-prem HSM.

[04:28] Priya: how do you handle graceful degradation at the model level? we want deterministic fallbacks not random.
[04:35] Omar: routing policies can be policy-driven: latency SLO-first routes to fastest variant, cost-first can route to quantized variant. for storms we offer automatic fallback to compatible model family and a hosted fallback tier with sanitized logs. policies are pluggable per-route.

[05:02] Lena: and regarding isolation — we need strong tenant fencing. our regulators would expect no cross-tenant leakage and demonstrable isolation. how do you guarantee that?
[05:13] Maya: Dedicated nodes are per-customer; within a cluster we provide tenant fencing via container isolation and NVidia MPS or ML framework-level partitioning. for highest assurance we recommend private deployment with bare-metal isolation. we'll include an architecture diagram in the security pack.

[05:42] Derek: fallback question — if we lose Dedicated capacity, do we get auto-failover to hosted? and how does that impact billing?
[05:52] Omar: yes, you can configure automatic fallback to hosted model variants in another region; fallback is a separate billing path (hosted usage). billing can be set to meter fallback usage and we can put thresholds to alert before failover.

[06:10] Marcus: latency SLO — we need p95 < 120ms for short path. can Dedicated meet that under peak?
[06:18] Omar: depends on batch sizing and prewarm. With properly sized warm-pool and continuous batching tuned to short token lengths, p95 of ~80–100ms is achievable on Ampere A10/A1-class GPUs. We'll validate with your exact traffic profile.

[06:37] Priya: what about quantized models for cost savings — how big is the quality delta for summarization?
[06:44] Omar: small but measurable; for structured financial summaries the delta can be mitigated with prompt engineering and reranking. We can run A/B evals as part of the POC.

[07:02] Lena: ok, procurement — we need pricing scenarios ready by friday. our Q2 budget decision meeting is next Monday. can you align?
[07:12] Maya: yes we'll prioritize. Maya: action — produce quarterly-aligned pricing scenarios and recommended warm-pool sizes based on estimated spikes. Omar will get the bench plan out tomorrow.

[07:26] Omar: for the bench, we'll ask you for a traffic generator (or we can reuse your logs). plan: 2-hour run with periodic 10x spikes, measure p50/p95/p99, and test warm-pool vs no-warm-pool. also test fallback to hosted variant under simulated eviction.

[07:48] Marcus: we'll provide traffic profile. one ask — can the bench simulate KV cache hit rates? our cache hit rate is around 65% for short-paths.
[07:57] Omar: yes we can parameterize hit rates; that'll affect token compute. include that in the traffic artifact.

[08:08] Derek: two more procurement notes: SLA expectations for Dedicated (uptime), and termination notice. we normally require 60-day termination window for multi-quarter commits.
[08:20] Maya: SLA is available for Dedicated; we can draft contract terms and include typical termination and SLAs.

[08:30] Priya: what about observability — can we get token-level cost breakdowns per model route and alerts when we hit fallback thresholds?
[08:38] Omar: yes the console supports per-route token and latency breakdowns, and you can attach tracing hooks. alerts on fallback thresholds are configurable.

[08:52] Lena: any regulatory gotchas for us if we go private vs dedicated hosted? we're handling regulated financial data and likely need on-prem in some regions.
[09:03] Omar: Private gives you the most control — you host inference in your VPC or on-prem; control plane can still be Redwood-managed or customer-managed. We'll enumerate residual responsibilities in the security pack.

[09:18] Maya: before we wrap — quick recap: deliver pricing scenarios aligned to quarterly invoicing, security docs (SOC2/KMS/onprem), bench plan for 2-hour spike sim, and schedule a deep technical session next week focused on warm-pool sizing and eviction handling.
[09:33] Lena: that's right. also include fallback cost estimates (if we fall back to hosted for 30 minutes during a big launch, what's the bill impact).
[09:42] Omar: we'll include a fallback cost example.

[09:48] Derek: timeline — can we get pricing by fri 2025-04-03?
[09:52] Maya: yes.

[10:00] Marcus: i'll upload the synthetic generator / traffic profile to the shared drive by wednesday.
[10:05] Priya: and we'll pick a list of ~5 prompt templates/seed inputs for the A/B evals.

[10:12] Maya: excellent, thanks everyone. last call out: we discussed competitor comparison — apexai tends to push single-tenant boxes but less of the routing/fallback policy; cloudmodelz has aggressive discounts but limited private deployment options. will include notes.

[10:32] Lena: thanks, talk soon.
[10:35] Maya: thanks all. (call ends)

Notes / links referenced:
- shared doc: https://redwood.example.com/docs/galactic-burst-modeling
- security pack (SOC2/KMS/onprem) to be attached in follow-up email

End of transcript.
